redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: ITU DataHub records Lesotho's 4G/LTE population coverage at 85.1% (2024), which falls in the 75-89% band rather than 90%+. The 95.8%/98% figures in the cited slide deck describe overall/3G mobile network coverage, not LTE specifically, so the code is revised down to 4.

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Lesotho Communications Authority's 2023 national ICT household survey found 58.4% of individuals use the internet, and World Bank data shows 51.8% for 2024 (up from 48.99% in 2023); both figures sit within the 50-69% band, supporting the original code.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: Active LIXP in Maseru with 5 ISPs, 2 CDNs, revamped 2026
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. LIXP's own site and PeeringDB list Econet, Vodacom, LEC, NUL and government ministries as peers, and The Reporter (Feb 2026) confirms the LCA-hosted exchange serves five ISPs and two CDNs with an active upgrade project — consistent with an active IXP with moderate participation.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 92.7% cited is GSMA/DataReportal's connections-per-population figure (SIM-based, includes multi-SIM users), not unique subscriber penetration as the variable requires. World Bank data puts mobile subscribers at 69.35 per 100 people (2023), and the 2023 LCA national ICT survey found 83.1% of the population aged 15+ own a mobile phone; scaled to total population this implies penetration closer to 55-65%. Revised down to the 55-69% band and flagged for human review since no primary GSMA unique-subscriber figure could be directly verified.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with stronger evidence. The 2023 LCA national ICT survey found 66% of mobile-owning individuals (68.2% of recent users) have a smartphone, and Vodacom's 2023 ESG snapshot (citing Fitch Solutions) cites 67.7% smartphone penetration — both within the 60-79% band, replacing the original ITU broadband-penetration proxy with direct smartphone-ownership data.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The Data Protection Act (2011/2012) is in force, but multiple independent 2025 sources (Mayet & Associates law firm, CIPESA and the Government of Lesotho's own news release) confirm the Data Protection Commission/Commissioner it establishes has never been appointed and is not operational. This contradicts the "DPA established" claim; revised down to "legislation enacted but no enforcement authority" (code 3).

Comments: Small Vodacom facilities in Maseru, gov DC in Mohale's Hoek
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.

Code 2 confirmed on this replacement evidence, though the specific Mohale's Hoek government facility could not be independently verified — recommend human review of that detail.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Comments: Active policy, WB projects, mini-grids deploying
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.

As of September 2024, OnePower's donor-backed Sotho Minigrid Portfolio was expanding solar-battery mini-grids to over 9,100 rural households, and a new mini-grid regulatory framework (led by the Department of Energy/LEWA with GET.transform) was under parliamentary review as of November 2025 — indicating continued active policy development with real, if still limited, deployment.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original source was only a survey catalogue page with no outage figures. The actual World Bank Enterprise Surveys 2023 country profile reports 1.9 electrical outages per month for Lesotho (versus 2.3-8.3 for regional/income comparators), which corresponds to "moderate (monthly outages, occasional disruptions)" rather than weekly outages; revised to code 3.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with an updated source. The 2025 World Bank National Energy Compact shows domestic installed generation capacity of ~104.7MW is almost entirely renewable (72MW Muela hydro, 30MW Ramarothole solar, ~0.5MW other renewables, versus only 0.4MW diesel), consistent with the 75%+ band. Flagged for human review: roughly half of Lesotho's electricity consumption is met by imports from South Africa's largely coal-fired grid, so the renewable share of total electricity supplied (as opposed to domestically generated) is materially lower than this figure implies.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The stated code (3, "High", 0.50-0.64) directly contradicted the comment's own cited EGDI of 0.4414, which sits in the "Middle" band (0.25-0.49) — an internal inconsistency in the original row. The UN E-Government Survey 2024 confirms Lesotho remains in the middle EGDI/OSI group (ranked 145 of 193, per a September 2025 Internet Society Lesotho policy paper citing the 2024 survey), so the code is corrected to 2.

Definition: The gap between men and women in mobile internet usage or internet access. Based on the GSMA Mobile Gender Gap data or ITU gender-disaggregated ICT statistics. A smaller gap indicates more equitable access to digital opportunities.
Comments: 29% gap Sub-Saharan mobile internet (GSMA LMIC data)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited 29% figure is a Sub-Saharan Africa regional average from a GSMA LMIC-focused report, not Lesotho-specific. Lesotho's own national ICT survey (LCA, citing ITU's Measuring Digital Development 2023) found internet-use penetration of 59.9% for men versus 54.8% for women — a gap of only 5.1 percentage points — and a mobile-ownership gender gap of just 0.6 points. This is near parity (<10% gap); revised from code 2 to code 5.
